module.name: System.Threading
module.short: Task-based parallel programming library (thread pools, tasks, futures, and parallel loops)

descr.p: System.Threading implements a Delphi-compatible Parallel Programming Library (PPL) for Free Pascal. Instead of manually managing operating-system threads (TThread), applications express concurrency in terms of lightweight tasks (, ), typed asynchronous results (), and data-parallel loops ().

Work items are scheduled across a work-stealing thread pool () that reuses worker threads, balances uneven workloads via per-thread work-stealing queues, and propagates unhandled exceptions to the waiting caller inside a flattened .

element.name: EAggregateException
element.short: Aggregates one or more exceptions raised by concurrent tasks or parallel loop iterations

descr.p: EAggregateException collects exceptions thrown by asynchronous tasks (, ) or parallel loop replicas (, ). Nested aggregate exceptions are automatically flattened into a single list of inner exceptions.
Iterate over the collected exceptions using a for..in loop (which yields exactly Count elements), index them via InnerExceptions, or filter handled exceptions with Handle.

element.name: EAggregateException.Count
element.short: Number of inner exceptions contained in the aggregate exception

element.name: EAggregateException.InnerExceptions
element.short: Indexed access (0..Count - 1) to the captured exceptions

element.name: EAggregateException.GetEnumerator
element.short: Returns an enumerator over the 0..Count - 1 inner exceptions

element.name: EAggregateException.Handle
element.short: Invokes a predicate for each inner exception and re-raises any unhandled exceptions

element.name: TThreadPool
element.short: Work-stealing thread pool that executes queued tasks and parallel loops

descr.p: TThreadPool manages a set of reusable worker threads and a background monitor thread. Each worker thread maintains a local work-stealing queue alongside the global queue; idle workers steal pending work items from other threads before blocking on the queue event.

All worker threads and the monitor thread are owned by the pool (FreeOnTerminate = False). When a worker finishes, it moves to an internal finished-thread list and is joined (WaitFor) and freed by the monitor thread or during . Consequently, Pool.Free guarantees that no pool thread is still executing user code, destructors, or RTL thread epilogues after destruction returns.
Note: executes in the terminating worker thread before it is joined. Avoid calling TThread.Synchronize from OnThreadTerminate if the pool may be destroyed from the main thread.

element.name: TThreadPool.Default
element.short: Process-wide default thread pool used when no explicit pool is supplied

element.name: TThreadPool.Destroy
element.short: Signals shutdown, wakes all workers, joins and frees all worker and monitor threads

element.name: TThreadPool.SetMinWorkerThreads
element.short: Sets the minimum number of worker threads maintained by the pool

element.name: TThreadPool.SetMaxWorkerThreads
element.short: Sets the maximum number of concurrent worker threads allowed in the pool

element.name: TThreadPool.QueueWorkItem
element.short: Queues a procedure or method for asynchronous execution on the pool

element.name: TThreadPool.OnThreadTerminate
element.short: Callback invoked on a worker thread just before it terminates

element.name: ITask
element.short: Interface representing an asynchronous unit of work

descr.p: ITask provides lifecycle control (, , ) and status inspection () for asynchronous tasks managed by .

element.name: ITask.Wait
element.short: Blocks until the task completes, the timeout expires, or the task faults/cancels

descr.p: Wait checks completion using an acquire read barrier on the fast path before waiting on the completion event. If the task or any of its child replicas raised an unhandled exception, Wait raises an . If the task was canceled, Wait raises EOperationCancelled.

element.name: ITask.Start
element.short: Schedules the task for execution on its associated thread pool

element.name: ITask.Cancel
element.short: Requests cancellation of the task

element.name: ITask.Status
element.short: Current execution status of the task (TTaskStatus)

element.name: IFuture
element.short: Generic interface representing an asynchronous computation that produces a typed value

descr.p: IFuture<T> extends with a Value property that waits for completion if necessary and returns the computed result of type T (or re-raises any captured exception).

element.name: IFuture.Value
element.short: Waits for the computation to finish and returns its result

element.name: TTask
element.short: Factory and implementation class for asynchronous tasks and futures

descr.p: TTask provides class methods to create and start tasks (, ), start typed asynchronous functions (), and synchronize across task arrays (, ).

element.name: TTask.Run
element.short: Creates and immediately starts an asynchronous task

element.name: TTask.Future
element.short: Creates and immediately starts a typed asynchronous function returning IFuture<T>

element.name: TTask.WaitForAll
element.short: Waits for all tasks in the array to complete within an optional timeout

element.name: TTask.WaitForAny
element.short: Waits for at least one task in the array to complete and returns its index (-1 on timeout)

element.name: TParallel
element.short: Static class providing data-parallel loops (For) and fork-join task execution (Join)

descr.p: TParallel partitions iteration ranges () and heterogeneous procedure lists () across a using self-replicating tasks and dynamic stride sizing.

element.name: TParallel.For
element.short: Executes a loop range (Integer or Int64) in parallel across the thread pool

descr.p: TParallel.For partitions the inclusive range [aLowInclusive..aHighInclusive] into dynamically sized strides. Each worker claims a range atomically together with the stride value for that batch, ensuring that every iteration in a completed loop executes exactly once.

Overloads accepting a parameter provide each worker replica with its own state instance to request early loop termination via Break (ordered: all iterations below the lowest break index still run) or Stop (immediate: all replicas exit as soon as possible).

If one or more iterations raise an exception, the loop transitions to the faulted state, stops scheduling new iterations, collects the exceptions from all worker replicas, and raises a flattened in the calling thread.

element.name: TParallel.Join
element.short: Creates and starts a task that executes multiple procedures or events in parallel

descr.p: TParallel.Join schedules an array of procedures (TProcRef) or TNotifyEvent handlers concurrently on the thread pool and returns the started . Call .Wait on the returned task to block until all joined procedures finish.

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState
element.short: Per-replica loop control object passed to TParallel.For iterations

descr.p: TLoopState allows an iteration body of to cooperate with other worker threads:

ul.li: Break records the current iteration index as a candidate for LowestBreakIteration and prevents workers from starting iterations above that index, while guaranteeing that all iterations prior to the lowest break index still execute.
Stop signals all worker threads to stop executing further iterations immediately; LowestBreakIteration remains Null.
ShouldExit returns True when any replica has called Stop, raised an exception, or called Break at an index lower than the current iteration.

element.name: TParallel.TLoopResult
element.short: Completion summary returned by TParallel.For

descr.p: Completed is True when the loop ran all iterations without calling Break or Stop. When terminated via Break, LowestBreakIteration contains the smallest iteration index that invoked Break; when terminated via Stop (or completed normally), LowestBreakIteration is Null.
